name: Cardiovascular system
description: The heart, blood vessels and blood: the chambers, valves and coronary arteries, how the heartbeat is started and timed, the large arteries and veins of the neck and trunk, the two circuits, and the blood itself. Picture questions show the heart and large vessels, drawn see-through, with one part highlighted to name.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: About how big is the adult heart?
answers: About the size of a fist
wrong: About the size of a tennis ball
About the size of two fists
About the size of a grapefruit
questions.explanation: Roughly 300 g. It lies in the middle of the chest (the mediastinum), with its tip (apex) pointing down and to the left.

figure.alt: The heart seen from the front
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which way does the apex of the heart point?
questions.explanation: It beats against the chest wall at the fifth intercostal space, in line with the middle of the collarbone: the apex beat.

questions.prompt: What is the double-walled sac around the heart called?
questions.explanation: A tough outer fibrous layer and an inner serous layer, with a little fluid between to let the heart move without friction.

questions.prompt: What is it called when fluid or blood collecting in the pericardial sac squeezes the heart so it cannot fill?
questions.explanation: A medical emergency. The tough fibrous pericardium cannot stretch.

questions.prompt: From outside to inside, what are the three layers of the heart wall?
questions.explanation: The thick middle layer, the myocardium, is the cardiac muscle. The endocardium is the smooth lining that is continuous with the lining of the vessels.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does the heart have?
questions.explanation: Two atria above and two ventricles below.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the atria?
answers: To receive blood returning to the heart
wrong: To pump blood to the body
To pump blood to the lungs
questions.explanation: Their walls are thin, because they only push blood down into the ventricles.

questions.prompt: Which chambers are the pumping chambers that send blood out of the heart?
questions.explanation: The right ventricle sends blood to the lungs and the left ventricle to the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: Why is the wall of the left ventricle about three times thicker than the right?
answers: It has to pump blood round the whole body
It pumps to the whole body
wrong: It receives blood from the lungs
questions.explanation: The systemic circuit has much higher resistance than the lungs.

questions.prompt: What are the ear-shaped flaps on the top of each atrium called?
questions.explanation: They add a little to the atria's capacity. The left one is a common site of clots in atrial fibrillation.

questions.prompt: What wall separates the right and left sides of the heart?
questions.explanation: The interatrial septum between the atria and the interventricular septum between the ventricles.

questions.prompt: What is the dip in the wall between the atria, where a fetal hole closed at birth, called?
questions.explanation: In the fetus the foramen ovale lets blood bypass the lungs. If it does not close, the person has a patent foramen ovale.

questions.prompt: Which two large veins bring oxygen-poor blood into the right atrium?
answers: Superior vena cava and inferior vena cava
questions.explanation: The coronary sinus also drains the heart's own blood into it.

questions.prompt: Which vessels bring oxygen-rich blood into the left atrium?
questions.explanation: Usually four of them, two from each lung. They are the only veins that carry oxygen-rich blood.

questions.prompt: What is the path of blood through the heart, starting from the right atrium?
answers: Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, aorta
wrong: Right atrium, mitral valve, right ventricle, aortic valve, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium, tricuspid valve, left ventricle, pulmonary valve, aorta
Right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle, lungs, aorta
Right ventricle, right atrium, lungs, left ventricle, left atrium, aorta
questions.explanation: Right side: body to lungs. Left side: lungs to body.

questions.prompt: Which valves lie between the atria and the ventricles?
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve on the right and the mitral (bicuspid) valve on the left.

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Between the right atrium and right ventricle, with three cusps. The heart wall is drawn see-through.

figure.alt: The heart, drawn see-through, with a valve in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Between the left atrium and left ventricle, with two cusps. Named for its resemblance to a bishop's mitre.

figure.alt: The heart, drawn see-through, with a valve in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many cusps does the mitral valve have?
questions.explanation: That is why it is also called the bicuspid valve. The tricuspid valve and the semilunar valves have three.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the mitral valve in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: At the exit of the right ventricle, to the pulmonary trunk. It has three half-moon cusps.

figure.alt: The heart, drawn see-through, with a valve in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the aortic and pulmonary valves called, from the shape of their cusps?
questions.explanation: Half-moon pockets that fill and snap shut when blood tries to flow back.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the pulmonary valve in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the thin cords that stop the cusps of the atrioventricular valves from flipping back into the atria?
questions.explanation: They join the cusps to the papillary muscles, which pull on them as the ventricle contracts.

questions.prompt: Which structures are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Finger-like muscles on the ventricle wall, which pull on the chordae tendineae to hold the valve cusps shut.

figure.alt: The heart, drawn see-through, with parts in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles on the inside of the ventricles tighten the cords of the atrioventricular valves as the heart beats?
questions.explanation: If one ruptures, for example in a heart attack, the valve leaks badly.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the papillary muscles in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What causes the 'lub-dub' sounds of the heartbeat?
questions.explanation: 'Lub' is the atrioventricular valves closing as the ventricles contract; 'dub' is the semilunar valves closing as they relax. A leaky or narrowed valve causes a murmur.

questions.prompt: What is a valve that fails to open fully, so it blocks the flow of blood, called?
questions.explanation: A valve that leaks back is called regurgitant (incompetent).

questions.prompt: Narrowing of the aortic valve forces which chamber to work harder and thicken?
Which vessel do the coronary arteries branch from?
answers: The aorta, just above the aortic valve
questions.explanation: Just above the aortic valve, from the pockets behind two of its cusps (the aortic sinuses). They fill while the ventricle relaxes.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the coronary arteries in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which vessels are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: They run over the surface of the heart, feeding its muscle.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It runs in the groove between the right atrium and ventricle, with branches to the back of the heart.

figure.alt: The heart, with a coronary artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It splits at once into the anterior interventricular (left anterior descending) branch and the circumflex branch.

figure.alt: The heart, with a coronary artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which branch of the left coronary artery runs down the front of the heart in the groove between the ventricles?
questions.explanation: A blockage in it is nicknamed the 'widow-maker', because it feeds so much of the left ventricle and the septum.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the left coronary artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A branch of the left coronary artery wrapping round the left side of the heart in the groove between the left atrium and ventricle.

figure.alt: The heart, with a coronary artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the death of heart muscle from a blocked coronary artery called?
questions.explanation: Angina is the chest pain from a short shortage of blood that doesn't kill muscle.

questions.prompt: What is chest pain from heart muscle that is short of blood but not yet dying called?
questions.explanation: Typically it comes on with effort and goes with rest.

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It runs up beside the anterior interventricular artery, then wraps round to the back to join the coronary sinus.

figure.alt: The heart, with a cardiac vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A wide vein on the back of the heart that collects most of its blood and empties it into the right atrium. Seen here from behind.

figure.alt: The heart from behind, with a vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In order, how does the electrical impulse pass through the heart?
answers: SA node, AV node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibres
wrong: AV node, SA node, bundle of His, Purkinje fibres, bundle branches
SA node, bundle of His, AV node, Purkinje fibres, bundle branches
Purkinje fibres, bundle branches, bundle of His, AV node, SA node
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial node starts it, the atria contract, the atrioventricular node delays it briefly, then it fans out through the ventricles from the bottom up.

questions.prompt: Which small patch of cells in the right atrium is the heart's natural pacemaker?
questions.explanation: It fires about 60 to 100 times a minute on its own. The vagus nerve slows it and the sympathetic nerves speed it up.

questions.prompt: Why does the atrioventricular node delay the impulse briefly?
answers: So the atria finish emptying into the ventricles first
To let the ventricles fill first
questions.explanation: About a tenth of a second.

questions.prompt: What does the P wave of an ECG show?
questions.explanation: QRS is the ventricles depolarising (and the atria repolarising, hidden within it); the T wave is the ventricles repolarising.

questions.prompt: What does the QRS complex of an ECG show?
What structures join cardiac muscle cells end to end, so the whole heart contracts together?
questions.explanation: They have gap junctions that let the electrical signal pass from cell to cell.

questions.prompt: How is cardiac output calculated?
questions.explanation: About 70 beats a minute × 70 mL = roughly 5 litres a minute at rest, about the whole blood volume every minute.

questions.prompt: What is the amount of blood one ventricle pumps with each beat called?
questions.explanation: About 70 mL at rest.

questions.prompt: What is the phase of the heartbeat when the ventricles contract called?
questions.explanation: Diastole is the relaxation, when they fill.

questions.prompt: In a blood pressure of 120/80, what does the 80 measure?
questions.explanation: The 120 is the systolic pressure, at the peak of the beat.

questions.prompt: Closure of which valves makes the first heart sound ('lub')?
What is the defining feature of an artery?
answers: It carries blood away from the heart
Carries blood away from the heart
questions.explanation: Usually the blood is oxygen-rich, but the pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.

questions.prompt: From inside to outside, what are the three layers of an artery's wall?
answers: Tunica intima, tunica media, tunica externa
Tunica intima, tunica media, tunica adventitia
wrong: Tunica externa, tunica media, tunica intima
Tunica media, tunica intima, tunica externa
questions.explanation: The intima is the smooth lining (endothelium), the media is smooth muscle and elastic tissue (thicker in arteries), and the externa is connective tissue (also called the adventitia).

questions.prompt: Why are the aorta's walls full of elastic fibres?
answers: They stretch with each beat and recoil to keep the blood flowing
wrong: To let it carry more blood
To let it contract like muscle
questions.explanation: The recoil during diastole keeps the blood moving between beats. Hardening of the arteries (arteriosclerosis) loses this.

questions.prompt: What is the build-up of fatty plaque in the walls of arteries called?
questions.explanation: It narrows the arteries and can lead to heart attack and stroke.

questions.prompt: What is a bulge in an artery wall, which may burst, called?
questions.explanation: The aorta and the arteries at the base of the brain are common sites.

questions.prompt: Which vessels control how much blood goes to each tissue by narrowing and widening?
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle in their walls allows this. They are the main control of blood pressure (resistance).

questions.prompt: Where does the exchange of oxygen, nutrients and wastes between blood and tissues take place?
questions.explanation: Their walls are only one cell thick.

questions.prompt: What are the parts of the aorta, in order from the heart?
answers: Ascending aorta, aortic arch, descending aorta
wrong: Descending aorta, aortic arch, ascending aorta
Aortic arch, ascending aorta, descending aorta
Ascending aorta, descending aorta, aortic arch
questions.explanation: The descending aorta is the thoracic aorta above the diaphragm and the abdominal aorta below it.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the aorta in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The body's biggest artery, from the left ventricle down to the pelvis, where it splits into the common iliac arteries.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the aorta in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The first part of the aorta, rising from the left ventricle. The coronary arteries come off it.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with part of the aorta in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The bend of the aorta over the left lung's root, with three branches: the brachiocephalic trunk, the left common carotid and the left subclavian arteries.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with part of the aorta in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In order, what are the three branches of the aortic arch?
answers: Brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery
wrong: Left common carotid, brachiocephalic trunk, left subclavian
Right subclavian, right common carotid, left common carotid
Left subclavian, left common carotid, brachiocephalic trunk
questions.explanation: Only three branches for the head, neck and both arms. The brachiocephalic trunk splits into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the aortic arch in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the end of the arch, down through the chest and the abdomen.

figure.alt: The aorta and its branches, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: At about which vertebral level does the aorta divide into the two common iliac arteries?
questions.explanation: The level of the top of the iliac crests.

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The first branch of the aortic arch. It divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries. There is no left one.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with an artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Runs up the front of the neck beside the windpipe, and divides near the top of the thyroid cartilage.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with an artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which artery can you feel pulsing beside the windpipe on the side of the neck?
questions.explanation: Never press both at the same time: pressing the carotid sinus can slow the heart and drop the blood pressure.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the common carotid artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The common carotid artery divides into which two arteries?
questions.explanation: The internal carotid supplies the brain and the eye; the external carotid supplies the face, scalp and neck.

questions.prompt: Which arteries, running through the transverse foramina of the cervical vertebrae, join to form the basilar artery?
questions.explanation: Branches of the subclavian arteries. They supply the back of the brain.

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Passes under the collarbone (sub-clavian) on its way to the arm. It becomes the axillary artery at the first rib.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with an artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In order, what are the arteries of the arm, from the subclavian artery down?
questions.explanation: The subclavian becomes the axillary at the first rib, the brachial at the lower border of teres major, and splits at the elbow into radial and ulnar.

questions.prompt: Which artery is listened to with a stethoscope when taking blood pressure?
questions.explanation: In the crook of the elbow, on the inner side of the biceps tendon.

questions.prompt: Which artery is felt at the wrist, on the thumb side, to take the pulse?
Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Leaves the right ventricle and splits into the right and left pulmonary arteries, which carry oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with a vessel in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which arteries carry oxygen-poor blood?
questions.explanation: And the pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood. The terms artery and vein say which way the blood goes, not what it carries.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the pulmonary trunk in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The first branch of the abdominal aorta, just below the diaphragm. It splits at once into three.

figure.alt: The abdominal aorta, with an artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the three branches of the celiac trunk?
answers: Left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries
wrong: Superior mesenteric, inferior mesenteric and renal
Right gastric, splenic and cystic arteries
questions.explanation: It supplies the foregut: the stomach, spleen, liver, gallbladder, pancreas and the first part of the duodenum.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the celiac trunk and its branches in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which artery and its branches are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The celiac trunk with the common hepatic, splenic and left gastric arteries.

figure.alt: The abdominal aorta, with an artery and its branches in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Leaves the aorta below the celiac trunk and supplies the small intestine and the first half of the large intestine.

figure.alt: The abdominal aorta, with an artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small branch low on the aorta. It supplies the second half of the large intestine, from the left side of the colon to the rectum.

figure.alt: The abdominal aorta, with an artery in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which three unpaired arteries of the abdominal aorta supply the digestive tract?
answers: Celiac, superior mesenteric and inferior mesenteric
Celiac trunk, superior mesenteric, inferior mesenteric
questions.explanation: Foregut, midgut and hindgut, from top to bottom.

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Short, wide branches of the abdominal aorta to the kidneys. Together the kidneys get about a fifth of the cardiac output.

figure.alt: The abdominal aorta and kidneys' vessels, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The aorta's two end branches, each dividing into the external and internal iliac arteries.

figure.alt: The vessels of the pelvis, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Runs along the pelvic brim, under the inguinal ligament, where it becomes the femoral artery to the thigh.

figure.alt: The vessels of the pelvis, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Dives into the pelvis to supply the pelvic organs and the buttock.

figure.alt: The vessels of the pelvis, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In order, what are the arteries of the leg, from the external iliac artery down?
answers: Femoral, popliteal, then anterior and posterior tibial arteries
wrong: Popliteal, femoral, then anterior and posterior tibial
Femoral, tibial, popliteal, then dorsalis pedis
questions.explanation: The femoral artery becomes the popliteal behind the knee. Below the knee it splits into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.

questions.prompt: Which artery is felt in the middle of the groin, just under the inguinal ligament?
questions.explanation: A common site to take blood and a pulse in an emergency, and the entry point for many catheters.

questions.prompt: Which artery is felt on the top of the foot to check the circulation of the leg?
questions.explanation: The continuation of the anterior tibial artery. It is absent in a few people.

questions.prompt: Which pair of arteries supplies the front of the brain, and which pair (joined into the basilar artery) the back?
answers: Internal carotids supply the front, vertebrals the back
wrong: Vertebrals the front, carotids the back
External carotids the front, subclavians the back
Both pairs supply the front only
questions.explanation: They join at the base of the brain to form the circle of Willis.

questions.prompt: Which vein carries blood from the intestines, spleen and pancreas to the liver?
questions.explanation: Formed by the union of the splenic vein and the superior mesenteric vein behind the neck of the pancreas. It brings nutrients to the liver before the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: What is the defining feature of a vein?
answers: It carries blood towards the heart
wrong: It carries blood to the capillaries
questions.explanation: Usually the blood is oxygen-poor, but the pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood.

questions.prompt: What stops blood flowing backwards in the veins of the limbs?
questions.explanation: Together with the squeezing of nearby muscles (the muscle pump) and the breathing movements, they push blood up towards the heart.

questions.prompt: What are swollen, twisted veins from failed valves called?
questions.explanation: Most often in the superficial veins of the legs.

questions.prompt: About how much of the body's blood is in the veins at any time?
questions.explanation: Their thin, stretchy walls make them a reservoir (capacitance vessels). The arteries hold about 15%.

questions.prompt: What is a blood clot in a deep leg vein called?
questions.explanation: If a piece breaks off it travels through the right heart to the lungs and blocks a pulmonary artery: a pulmonary embolism.

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Formed behind the first right costal cartilage by the two brachiocephalic veins; it drains the head, neck, arms and chest into the right atrium.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with a vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Formed by the two common iliac veins at L5, it runs up on the right of the aorta, through the diaphragm at T8, into the right atrium.

figure.alt: The large vessels of the trunk, with a vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Formed on each side by the internal jugular and subclavian veins. The left one is longer, crossing in front of the aortic arch's branches.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with a vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Drains the brain and the face and neck, running down the neck beside the common carotid artery.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with a vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Drains the arm and passes in front of the scalenus anterior, in front of the subclavian artery.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with a vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: A central line, a long catheter placed to give drugs near the heart, is often put into which vein?
questions.explanation: The tip rests in the superior vena cava, close to the right atrium.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the internal jugular vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which vessels are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Usually four of them, two from each lung, entering the back of the left atrium. Seen here from behind.

figure.alt: The heart from behind, with vessels in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Carries blood from the kidney into the inferior vena cava. The left one is longer than the right, because the vena cava lies to the right of the aorta.

figure.alt: The vessels of the kidneys, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Why is the left renal vein longer than the right?
answers: The inferior vena cava is on the right
The vena cava lies to the right of the aorta
It has to cross in front of the aorta
wrong: The right kidney has a shorter artery
questions.explanation: It crosses in front of the aorta, below the origin of the superior mesenteric artery, to reach it.

figure.alt: The heart and large vessels, with the renal veins in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The two join at the level of L5 to form the inferior vena cava.

figure.alt: The vessels of the pelvis, with a vein in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which veins are highlighted in red?
answers: Splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein
questions.explanation: They join behind the neck of the pancreas to form the hepatic portal vein.

figure.alt: The vessels of the abdomen, with veins in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which is the longest vein in the body, running up the inside of the leg?
questions.explanation: From the foot to the groin, where it joins the femoral vein. It is often taken for heart bypass grafts.

questions.prompt: Which superficial vein runs up the outer side of the arm, ending by joining the axillary vein?
questions.explanation: The basilic vein runs up the inner side. The median cubital vein joins them at the elbow, and is where blood is usually taken.

questions.prompt: Which vein in the crook of the elbow is most often used to take blood?
questions.explanation: It is large, close to the surface, and held in place by tissue, with fewer nerves and arteries nearby than the other veins at the elbow.

questions.prompt: Which vein runs up the right side of the thoracic vertebral column, draining the chest wall into the superior vena cava?
questions.explanation: An alternative route to the heart when the inferior vena cava is blocked.

questions.prompt: What does a raised jugular venous pressure (visible swollen neck veins) suggest?
answers: Raised pressure in the right atrium
Right-sided heart failure or fluid overload
questions.explanation: The neck veins connect without valves to the right atrium, so they show its pressure.

questions.prompt: Which circuit carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs and back to the left atrium?
questions.explanation: Short and low-pressure. The systemic circuit goes from the left ventricle to the rest of the body and back to the right atrium.

questions.prompt: What do we call a route where blood passes through two capillary beds in a row before going back to the heart, as in the liver?
questions.explanation: Blood from the gut capillaries goes through the liver's sinusoids before it reaches the heart.

questions.prompt: In the fetus, which vessel joins the pulmonary trunk to the aorta, skipping the lungs?
questions.explanation: It closes within hours or days of birth and becomes the ligamentum arteriosum.

questions.prompt: Which vessel of the umbilical cord carries oxygen-rich blood from the placenta to the fetus?
questions.explanation: The two umbilical arteries carry oxygen-poor blood back to the placenta. This is the opposite of the usual rule, which is why the terms say direction, not oxygen.

questions.prompt: About how much blood does an adult have?
questions.explanation: About 7% of body weight.

questions.prompt: About what share of blood is plasma?
questions.explanation: A pale yellow fluid, 90% water. The cells make up the rest.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
questions.explanation: Their haemoglobin binds oxygen. They have no nucleus, so they have more room.

questions.prompt: Which cell fragments help blood to clot?
questions.explanation: Made in the bone marrow by large cells called megakaryocytes.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells defend the body against infection?
questions.explanation: Neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils and basophils.

questions.prompt: Which is the most common white blood cell?
questions.explanation: About 60 to 70% of white cells. They are the first to arrive at an infection and eat bacteria.

questions.prompt: A person with blood group AB has which antibodies in their plasma against A or B?
questions.explanation: So they can receive blood of any ABO group (the universal recipient). Group O has both antibodies and no antigens, so its red cells can be given to any group.

questions.prompt: Which ABO blood group is called the universal donor for red cells?
questions.explanation: No A, B or Rh antigens on its red cells for the recipient's antibodies to attack.

questions.prompt: Which mineral at the centre of haemoglobin binds oxygen?
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.prompt: What is the last step of blood clotting, in which a soluble protein turns into a mesh of fibres?
questions.explanation: Thrombin, made from prothrombin, makes the change. Vitamin K is needed for the liver to make prothrombin and some other clotting factors.

questions.prompt: What is a clot or other lump that travels in the blood and blocks a smaller vessel called?
questions.explanation: A thrombus is a clot that stays where it formed.

questions.prompt: What is a stroke?
answers: Loss of blood supply to part of the brain
Death of brain tissue from a blocked or burst artery
wrong: Failure of the heart to pump
A sudden drop in blood pressure
questions.explanation: About 85% are from a blocked artery (ischaemic) and the rest from bleeding (haemorrhagic).

questions.prompt: Blood pressure persistently above what level is called high (hypertension)?
questions.explanation: Guidelines differ a little (some use 130/80). It often has no symptoms but raises the risk of stroke and heart disease.

questions.prompt: Which sensors in the aortic arch and carotid sinus detect changes in blood pressure?
questions.explanation: They signal the medulla through the vagus and glossopharyngeal nerves, which adjusts heart rate and vessel widths.

questions.prompt: Which system returns fluid that leaks from the capillaries back to the blood?
questions.explanation: It empties into the large veins at the base of the neck.
